This is not a blacklist: it is a cost filter. The ideator MUST read it before proposing, and any proposal sharing an axis with an entry here MUST name the revival condition it satisfies.

meta_rules.rule: SCOPED 2026-08-26 to the SYMMETRIC family. The old wording said 'the continuous/gradient family is exhausted' and that 'at Rocket's operating scale the better order is NOT preferred by the surrogate at ANY beta in [0.05, 1.05]'. Both clauses are FALSE outside odd-symmetric shapes g(-z)=1-g(z), and the counterexample was logged on 2026-08-17: H38's one-sided surrogate scores +0.36675 pp pure Rocket on connectome (3/3 seeds, 30.6x the minimum effect size), and Q05 measures its alignment at +1.48..+2.00 with NO crossover in beta*std over [1e-2,1e6]. THE RULE NOW READS: within the odd-symmetric family the continuous axis is exhausted, and any symmetric-shape hypothesis must explain how it escapes Q01's scale-blindness. An ASYMMETRIC objective is NOT covered: it does not telescope into the imbalance objective (its first-order term runs over the order-dependent VIOLATED subset), so Q01's collapse argument does not reach it. Such a hypothesis must still (a) pass src/mfas/analysis/surrogate_gate.py, (b) show no crossover in beta*std, and (c) be measured COMPOSED with the champion stack, not against pure Rocket -- because the one thing Q01 does not settle is whether a better pure order survives composition, and the measured pure->final transfer coefficient is 10-28% and turns NEGATIVE past the operating point (proto_S01_connectome.json). Fifteen shapes have been measured inside the symmetry assumption and exactly two outside it, both positive on the primary (H38 +0.36675, H38B +0.14416). ---- AMENDED 2026-08-27 (cycle 16, H64). THE OPEN CLAUSE IS NOW CLOSED, AND THE ANSWER IS AFFIRMATIVE. This rule required an asymmetric hypothesis to (a) pass surrogate_gate.py, (b) show no crossover in beta*std, and (c) be measured COMPOSED with the champion stack, 'because the one thing Q01 does not settle is whether a better pure order survives composition'. H64 did all three. It DOES survive: connectome pure 82.92969571752491 -> 83.23791666953974 (+0.308221 pp, i.e. 84% of H38's MPS random-init figure SURVIVES the greedy-FAS warm start, so the basin objection is answered too), and composed 84.15409511053134 -> 84.25817950936937 (+0.104084 pp, 8.67x the bar, 5/5 bit-identical seeds, at a LOWER wall clock). The measured pure->final transfer coefficient is 33.8%, ABOVE proto_S01's 10.3-28.0% band. So the sentence 'the measured pure->final transfer coefficient is 10-28% and turns NEGATIVE past the operating point' is not a bound on what a shape gain can deliver - it was measured by varying EPOCHS along one pipeline, and a shape change transfers better than an epoch change does. Requirements (a), (b) and (c) all STAND for any future asymmetric proposal. What is retired is the presumption that (c) would fail. H64 was NOT promoted, for reasons that have nothing to do with the mechanism (a missing relabelling study and a microns runtime failure that also affects the champion) - see experiments/log.md 2026-08-27 Cycle 16.

meta_rules.rule: Plain Rocket has no seed-to-seed score dispersion to harvest (connectome 82.8845 +/- 0.0225 pp) even though orderings differ (Spearman 0.958). Any best-of-K / multi-start / sampling idea must first show it CREATES score dispersion, or it harvests nothing.

A move class's own stage credit is NOT its contribution, and a prototype showing that a class 'works' is NOT a screen. Move classes inside an alternating refiner compete for the same ground. MEASURED 2026-08-16: H41's segment class was credited +0.07010 pp on connectome while delivering +0.00570 pp net, because adding it cut the two existing classes' joint credit from 0.24058 to 0.17618 - 91.9% of what it found was already reachable. Judge a new move class ONLY by the composed champion-vs-variant delta at constant-for-constant matched settings, and REPORT THE REDUNDANCY FRACTION (old classes' credit before minus after, over the new class's credit). A class must also clear the marginal rate of the stage it is inserted into (stage 4 measured at 3.45e-4 pp/s on connectome, 4.33e-4 on microns), not merely be non-zero.

NARROWED 2026-08-16 - read the amendment before citing this rule. PROVEN: bounded-window single-node local search is empty for W <= 100 (leakage-safe reachable pool at W=100 is 0.0270 pp of a 0.4606 pp remaining gap; H30's W=10 arm measured ~0). DIRECTIVE, still in force: prefer global-range or structurally decomposed (SCC / block) move classes. NOT PROVEN, and formerly asserted here as if it were: that windows ABOVE 100 are empty. The headline figures this rule used to quote (W=100 -0.010 pp, W=1000 -0.170, W=5000 -0.405) are measure2_gap_flip_distance.net_pp = gain(W) - lose(W) from experiments/size_localsearch.py. That statistic measures how much of the REFERENCE ordering's own rearrangement is short-range - a property of the reference, not a bound on local search. A hill-climb never pays the `lose` term, it declines those moves, so a negative net_pp does not imply nothing is recoverable. The leakage-safe CEILING in the same artifact (measure1_reachable_pool) puts the reachable feedback pool at 0.4141 pp for W=1000 and 2.3225 pp for W=5000, so CAPACITY IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT above W=100. A ceiling is not an achievable amount - flipping window edges creates new feedback. Do not cite Vahidi 2025 either way: that method is uncapped/global-range, not bounded-span (autoresearch/lit/vahidi-2025.md). RE-MEASURED FROM THE CHAMPION 2026-08-28 (cycle 21, H78), and it SURVIVES NARROWED. The percentiles this rule and findings.md #3 quote (p25=8,290 / p50=22,580 / p90=87,497) were computed on H02's 82.9161% order; 78.9% of that +1.6874 pp net gap has since been harvested. Recomputed by the SAME code (imported verbatim) on the H64 champion: p25=2,120 / p50=10,430 / p75=31,277 / p90=69,532. The median more than halved (ratio 0.4619), which CONFIRMS that the pipeline harvested the long-range component preferentially - but SHORTER IS NOT SHORT: p50=10,430 is still 7.6% of n=136,648, a W=1000 window holds only 18.23% of total gain and W=5000 only 36.51%. The directive ('prefer global-range or structurally decomposed move classes') therefore stands. What has changed is that M15 now supplies the reason the directive is not enough on its own. Evidence: experiments/outputs/proto_H78_connectome.json.

meta_rules.rule: The continuous optimizer leaves 0 exact position ties and negligible near-ties (0.03% vs a 1.69 pp gap). Nothing is recoverable from tie-breaking or strict-'>' handling. Permanently closed.

The init -> plateau curve is flat on connectome (82.87-82.93% across inits spanning 36-69% quality). Better-init-alone has a <=0.06 pp ceiling; H02 already took it. Init ideas only matter in combination with a mechanism that can HOLD the better basin.

Among discrete starting orders for the sift, cheap greedy-FAS is at least as good as expensive global linear-algebra embeddings. Trophic and magnetic-Laplacian warm-starts were both WORSE seeds, and the spectral one cost 304-507 s. Do not buy an expensive warm-start.

QUANTITATIVE form of M3, and it supersedes M3's existential test. Dispersion existing is not enough: best-of-R over R draws gains sigma * a_R over the mean (a_R = E[max of R standard normals]: a_2 = 0.5642, a_3 = 0.8463, a_4 = 1.0294), and R is NOT a free parameter - it is floor(runtime guard deadline / per-run wall clock). So a multi-start idea must show sigma >= min_promotion_delta_pp / a_R_feasible BEFORE it is built. On connectome at the champion's 1152.0 s/run the deadline allows R = 2, so the required sigma is 0.012 / 0.5641896 = 0.021269 pp. MEASURED relabelling sigma is 0.019124 pp - a 10% shortfall with no room to buy it back with R. Two corollaries. (1) The comparator is the CANONICAL score sota.json records, not the labelling mean; when canonical sits above the mean (here z = +1.029) best-of-R over RANDOM draws is a REGRESSION and only a canonical-anchored design is even monotone. (2) The matched-compute control is the measured saturation curve, not an assumption: doubling refinement seconds at ONE labelling buys +0.006275 pp against best-of-2's +0.000351 pp, i.e. ~18x more for the same clock. CAVEAT the rule carries with it: sigma is usually estimated from few points, and the chi-squared interval at n = 5 spans a factor of ~4.8 (here [0.011458, 0.054955] pp). Apply M9 to the point estimate to decide whether to BUILD, but do not call a kill secure on this ground alone unless the interval's relevant bound also clears - say which you used.

The relabelling nuisance of this pipeline is created almost entirely in the SHARED PREFIX (greedy-FAS tie-breaks -> Rocket), not in the refinement tail. MEASURED on connectome: whole-pipeline sigma 0.019124 pp (n = 5, proto_P09_connectome.json) vs TAIL-ONLY sigma 0.003731 pp from one fixed prefix (n = 8, proto_H57_connectome.json) - i.e. the tail holds ~4% of the variance and the prefix ~96%. CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this rule exists rather than being folded into M9: sharing the prefix to buy a bigger R is self-defeating. It multiplies R by about 2 (connectome R = 2 -> 4) while dividing sigma by about 5 (ratio 0.003731/0.019124 = 0.195), and a_R grows far too slowly to compensate - a_4/a_2 is only 1.82. So ANY design of the form 'pay the expensive prefix once, randomise the cheap tail R times' is dead on arithmetic before it is built, whatever the tail is. STRONGEST FORM OF THE EVIDENCE: over the nine measured arms the canonical labelling is the MAXIMUM, so the canonical-anchored best-of-R gains exactly 0.000000 pp at every R, by enumeration rather than by estimate. Together with M9 this closes the multi-start family: the only surviving door is a mechanism that WIDENS sigma at the champion's per-arm cost, and it has to widen the PREFIX's sigma, because that is where the dispersion is.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THIS CAMPAIGN IS ACHIEVABILITY, NOT CAPACITY - and the gap between them is about two orders of magnitude. M4's amendment asserted this in words ('a ceiling is not an achievable amount - flipping window edges creates new feedback'); H47 measured both numbers on the SAME order at the SAME scale for the first time. On the champion's connectome order, the weight of backward edges confined inside 16-node contiguous windows is +0.479839 pp - MORE than the entire remaining 0.4606 pp gap to the reference - yet the EXACT optimum over all k! orderings of those windows realises +0.004342 pp, which is 0.90% of it. microns 4.59%, mouse 1.95%. CONSEQUENCE, and this is the operative half: a 'reachable pool' / 'ceiling' / 'confined weight' statistic is NOT evidence that a move class will pay, and must never again be quoted as the justification for building one. It bounds the family from above and nothing more. The only admissible evidence is a realised gain from an exact or run optimum. Quote a ceiling only alongside its realisation ratio, and if the ratio is unmeasured, say so.
evidence: killed.json M4 amendment, which stated this without measuring it

meta_rules.rule: A COMPOSED PROTOTYPE RUN FROM THE CHAMPION'S OWN CONVERGED ORDER SYSTEMATICALLY OVERSTATES a pipeline change, because the control arm starts at (or near) its own fixed point and the variant arm does not. The variant harvests ground the real pipeline's control ALSO harvests - earlier in its own trajectory, where a from-champion control can no longer re-take it. So `champion order + N cycles of X` minus `champion order + N cycles of Y` is NOT an estimator of `full pipeline with X` minus `full pipeline with Y`. MEASURED on H60, prototype vs screen on the same mechanism: connectome +0.027477 -> +0.007311 pp (3.76x overstatement), microns +0.003448 -> +0.002967 (1.16x), mouse +0.085531 -> EXACTLY +0.000000 (the control arm there had 0.000000 pp left, and the full pipeline gained nothing at all). SECOND HALF, and it is why this is a rule and not an erratum: the prototype rung is biased in BOTH directions depending on where it starts. A standalone refiner measured from scratch UNDER-states (H36: one-shot condensation +0.00013 pp -> +0.1837 pp alternated); a composed variant measured from the champion's converged order OVER-states. The only unbiased measurement of a pipeline change is the pipeline. OPERATIVE CONSEQUENCE: a composed-from-champion prototype number is a SCREENING number - fine for deciding whether to spend GPU, never quotable as the expected screen result, and never as evidence in a promotion argument. Quote it with its control arm's own remaining headroom beside it, which is what makes the bias visible.

It therefore applies to a variant that changes an INNER stage (H60: prototype +0.027477 -> screen +0.007311, 3.76x) and NOT to one that only APPENDS a terminal stage. meta_rules.rule: A PERTURB-AND-REPAIR GAIN MEASURED ON AN OLDER, WEAKER BASE DOES NOT TRANSFER TO THE CURRENT CHAMPION, and must be re-measured there before it may motivate an item. MEASURED on one mechanism, both directions of the same grid: the ASYM gradient kick is worth +0.018620 pp attributable at base 83.91351804242117 and at best -0.020779 pp at base 84.25817950936937 - a SIGN REVERSAL across 0.344661 pp of base improvement. The reason is mechanical: a repair stage can only re-take ground the base has not already taken, so every improvement to the base consumes the repair's headroom. The diagnostic is CHEAP and should be run FIRST for any repair-shaped item - run the repair operator alone from the champion order and read its headroom. Here it was EXACTLY 0.000000 pp, which settled the item before any arm was run. RELATION TO M12: M12 says a from-champion prototype OVERSTATES an inner-stage change (mis-sited measurement); M13 says an INHERITED number from a superseded base overstates everything (out-of-date measurement). PRACTICAL FORM: an item whose prior_evidence is a delta on a superseded base has NO evidence until that delta is re-measured on the sitting champion. Queue items P25 and H75 exist to apply this to the standing queue.

WHERE INSIDE THE EXACT-OPTIMAL PLATEAU A MOVER IS SENT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR THE FINAL SCORE, because the stage-4 alternation absorbs it. The exact-gain insertion profile is piecewise-constant with at most deg(u) breakpoints over n gaps, so its maximum is attained on an INTERVAL, not a point: measured on a real connectome stage-3 trajectory, 95.0-99.7% of movers sit on a plateau of width > 1, median width 574-1,646 ranks. Replacing the production rule (leftmost maximizing gap) with the nearest maximizing gap redirects 44.0-74.9% of movers and cuts mean transport by 800-4,961 ranks per mover FOR THE SAME EXACT GAIN - and moves the final connectome score by -0.002271 pp, 19% of the bar. The mechanism of the null is measured, not assumed: stage 3 gets WORSE by -0.018505 pp (84.11761164861514 -> 84.09910627090132) and stage 4's increment grows by +0.016234 pp (0.14056786075423133 -> 0.15680182026491707), i.e. 87.7% ABSORPTION. NOTE THE SIGN: the leftward bias is load-bearing FOR THE SIFT and in the direction opposite to H73's hypothesis - over-transport helps stage 3 - but the pipeline does not care either way. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: any item whose mechanism changes a move's DESTINATION without changing its exact GAIN (same argmax set, a different point of it) must show it survives stage 4. The cheap diagnostic needs no new code - run one arm of each and read sift_best_pct and alt_increment_pp side by side in the run JSONs. M14 is the sibling of M8 (a move class's own stage credit is not its contribution), with the competitor being the SAME class at a later stage rather than a different one, and of M12 (a difference measured before the absorber is not the difference that ships). It also SCOPES M5: M5-no-ties is about CONTINUOUS position ties and does NOT generalise to the discrete profile, where plateaus are pervasive - the ties are real, they are just not worth anything.

meta_rules.rule: THE REFERENCE SOLUTION'S REMAINING ADVANTAGE OVER THE CHAMPION IS A PROPERTY OF THE WHOLE PERMUTATION AND OF NO PART OF IT, AND THE TWO ARE SEPARATED BY A BARRIER TWICE AS DEEP AS THE PRIZE. Measured from the H64 champion (84.25817950936937) against data/best_solution (84.61467764201586), residual +0.356498 pp. (1) THE DISAGREEMENT IS 6.7x THE PRIZE: gain +2.3787 pp / lose +2.0222 pp / net +0.3565 pp - the two orders disagree about the orientation of edges carrying 4.40 pp of weight and 85% of it cancels. At the H02 era the same ratio was 4.60/1.69 = 2.7:1, so the cancellation has become MORE severe as the score rose. 53.6% of nodes carry residual gain stake; median node displacement 6,051 ranks. This is Q02's flat degenerate near-optimal set, measured for the first time on the champion-vs-reference pair rather than seed-to-seed. (2) NO PARTIAL ADOPTION IS PROFITABLE, three probes: a linear rank-blend path ((1-t)*rank_champ + t*rank_best) runs through a VALLEY 0.786 pp DEEP at t=0.60 - 2.2x the 0.3565 pp prize and 66x the 0.012 pp promotion bar; teleporting the top-k highest-stake nodes to their reference rank loses at k=1 (-0.011753 pp) and monotonically to -4.737902 pp at k=30,000; and SLOT-PRESERVING adoption - subset re-ordered internally to the reference's opinion with ZERO collateral displacement of any other node - has a best proper subset of EXACTLY +0.000000 pp (a no-op) across three selection rules (stake, displacement, seeded random). Everything that changes anything, loses. CONSEQUENCE: from the champion's basin, NO MONOTONE PROCESS reaches the reference - not a better move class, not a longer ladder, not a cleverer tie-break. This is one mechanism for four separate nulls the campaign already had: M14's 87.7% stage-4 absorption, H66's 0.000000 pp repair headroom on the champion, H31's ILS/LNS null, and the <= +0.018 pp ceiling on every move class since H42. OPERATIVE DIRECTIVE: an item whose mechanism is a new or extended MONOTONE move class on the existing basin must now argue against M15 before it is scheduled, and the two surviving levels are a structurally DIFFERENT basin (H79) or a search that accepts uphill moves at ~0.8 pp scale (H80). SCOPE, and it is a real limit: two geometric families of partial adoption were tested, not all of them, so a valley along the blend path does not PROVE no path exists - the claim is evidential. Connectome-only: no reference solution exists for microns or mouse, the standing scope limit on all gap work (findings.md #3).

meta_rules.rule: THE CHAMPION PIPELINE'S CONNECTOME OUTPUT IS A PROPERTY OF THE GRAPH, NOT OF THE START. Measured on the H64 stack over FOUR cheap graph-structural constructions - greedy-FAS (the champion's), greedy-FAS on the transpose, static out_w-in_w sort, and SCC-condensation topological seeding - that span 2.406894 pp of initial quality (68.913428-71.320322 %) and sit Kendall tau 0.089885-0.432855 from the champion's construction, against a champion RELABELLING BALL whose own diameter is tau >= 0.937858. The FINAL scores span 0.005879 pp (84.25230054-84.25817951), i.e. the stack divides the input spread by 409x. THE CONTRACTION IS STAGE-WISE AND MONOTONE: 2.406894 pp (construction) -> 0.078483 pp after pure Rocket (30.7x) -> 0.009382 pp after the under-relaxed sift (8.4x) -> 0.005879 pp after stage 4 (1.6x). THREE CONSEQUENCES. (1) The multi-start family is closed on a THIRD independent axis, after H56 (relabelling) and H57 (prefix sharing): the champion's own construction is the MAXIMUM of the four by enumeration, so canonical-anchored best-of-basins gains EXACTLY 0.000000 pp at every R; and the basin-induced sample std is 0.003054 pp against M9/M10's 0.021269 pp bar - short by 7.0x, not a near miss. (2) M6 ('the init -> plateau curve is flat'), stated for plain Rocket at the 82.87-82.93 % plateau, SURVIVES THE WHOLE H64 STACK at 84.26 %: it is not an artefact of the weak 2026-06 pipeline. (3) It supplies a mechanism for M15 - a contraction cannot reach a point outside its image, whatever the start - and it is a fourth measured instance of the stack being NON-MONOTONE in input quality (reverse_greedy_fas leads pure Rocket by +0.078483 pp and finishes third of four; imbalance_sort starts +0.721 pp above greedy-FAS and finishes last; cf. H48 at +5.70387 pp). SCOPE, and it is a real limit: cheap graph-structural constructions only; imbalance_sort and scc_topo are tau = 0.874521 from EACH OTHER, so the four arms give ~three independent directions of contrast; connectome + mouse only (microns is in_screen: false and no variant losing on connectome can be promoted, so none was spent); and 'range over 4 points' is a downward-biased dispersion estimate - both it and the sample std clear the bar by wide margins, which is why the verdict does not turn on the choice. It says THIS stack erases the basin, not that the basin is irrelevant to a different one.

meta_rules.rule: ON THIS PROBLEM AN ACCEPTANCE SCHEDULE IS NOT A MECHANISM, BECAUSE BARRIER CROSSING IS BOUGHT IN ROUNDS AND ROUNDS ARE PRICED IN n. Crossing a barrier of depth D with a move class whose median downhill step is delta_med needs roughly D/delta_med consecutive ACCEPTED uphill moves, whose probability at T = c*delta_med is about exp(-D/(c*delta_med)); so the number of rounds required is exponential in D/delta_med while the number of rounds AVAILABLE inside a fixed wall budget falls with n. MEASURED on one move class (ruin-and-recreate + exact-gain reinsertion + a 2-sweep repair sift) across four instances spanning n = 148 to 136,648: the round rate is 1,106.99/s, 173.60/s, 15.91/s and 0.1467/s. From n=400 to n=136,648, n grows 342x and the round rate falls 1,183x. The consequence is a SIGN REVERSAL in the value of the temperature - it is worth +0.210785 pp at n=400, -0.019594 pp at n=4000 and -0.000072 pp on the connectome, where zero uphill moves were accepted at all - and a collapse in the deepest excursion the search can afford, from 4.32% of the measured barrier at n=400 to 0.10% at n=4000 to 0.00% on the connectome. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE CHEAP HALF: accepting EXACT-TIE sideways moves needs no temperature, no calibration and no hyperparameter, and it recovers 113.28% of the annealed arm's advantage at n=4000. meta_rules.rule: A MOVE CLASS CAN OWN ITS GROUND OUTRIGHT AND STILL LOSE, BECAUSE EXACT-GAIN EVALUATION IS PRICED IN THE MOVED SET'S DEGREES. This is M8's mirror image: M8 kills a class whose ground is already reachable (H41, 91.9% redundant); M18 kills a class whose ground is its OWN and whose per-candidate evaluation cost grew faster than its gain. MEASURED on H71 (cycle 24), connectome, from the H64 champion at a MATCHED 100,000-pop budget: enriching the interval repair from a positional cut - cost O(d(u)+d(v)), the H45/H52 pair move - to an arbitrary subset gamma - cost O(sum_{z in gamma} deg z), because the coupling term sum_{z in gamma, y in gamma_c, pos(y)<pos(z)}[w(z->y)-w(y->z)] must be evaluated - multiplied wall clock by 34.0x (45.0 s -> 1527.9 s) while multiplying realised gain by only 1.92x (+0.005655 pp -> +0.010870 pp). Richness buys gain SUB-LINEARLY in its own evaluation cost. The measured coupling cost was 65,575 edge visits per candidate, 9.4x the item's own a-priori ~7,000 estimate, so the cost side of such an item must be MEASURED on the real graph before it is scheduled, never estimated from mean degree. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: an item proposing a richer exact-gain move class must state its per-candidate evaluation cost as a function of the MOVED SET's degrees (not of the interval, and not of mean degree), and must show that cost times the pop count needed for convergence fits 3600 s. H61 (k-node joint re-insertion by subset DP) is the standing item this bites: its cost is O(sum deg * 2^k * k) - the same law with an extra 2^k - and it must answer before it is scheduled. It does NOT bite recombination (H82): partition crossover pays one O(n) scan plus one O(m) edge pass for the whole permutation, not a per-candidate degree sum.
